narrative_purpose: The cold-open image: the desolate Ashlands where a forest and a Hometree once stood, grounding the human stakes of the chapter's physics in the Mangkwan catastrophe.
subject: A wide desolate plain of black basalt and grey volcanic ash under a smoke-dimmed sky. In the middle distance stands the broken, blackened stump of a colossal fallen tree, its splintered crown collapsed. A few small Na'vi figures pick their way across the wasteland, tiny against the scale. On the far horizon a dull red glow marks distant volcanic vents; thin smoke drifts sideways.
scene: A ruined post-eruption landscape at grim overcast twilight, ash underfoot stretching to a low horizon, everything muted and grey-black except distant vent glow.
camera: Wide establishing shot low to the ash, the fallen Hometree stump as the focal landmark, tiny figures for scale.
light: Flat, smoke-dimmed daylight with almost no warmth; a scarce dull ember-red glow on the far horizon vents; cool grey-indigo overall.
palette: Dominant charcoal-black basalt and grey ash, cool indigo smoke sky, a single scarce dull ember-red horizon accent.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, textured ash and rock, bleak and atmospheric.
detail_level: Crisp on the ash textures and fallen stump near the viewer; the horizon and vents dissolving into smoke haze.
composition: Low horizon, the blackened Hometree stump on a third, small wandering figures leading the eye across the plain, wide dim sky above.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette but drained toward grey and black to read as ruined ash barrens. Na'vi figures tall and slender, kept small. Distinct from the warm glowing cover.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no lush forest, no bright sunlight, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon style
